newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday led by the bullish domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract soared to 30 percent from 16 percent last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 13.1 million lots from 9.52 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the surge of the domestic A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen boosted fund demand on the repo market. "The bullish A markets became the key factor today," one said.
Another reason for Monday's rise was the listing of two A share companies, one in Shanghai and one in Shenzhen, helping spur money demand, traders said.
"The rates will consolidate down on Tuesday because they are too high after today's surges," said a second trader.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down in dull trading and traders said the market was unlikely to recover in the short term due to the strong bull on the A share markets, which sucked funds out of the spot market.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 116.11 yuan from 116.25 yuan.
The combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 854,896 lots from 1.03 million lots.
Traders said the spot market was sluggish and both buyers and sellers were reluctant to trade.
"The market is short of captial, and if there is no fresh liquidity flowing in, prices will have a hard time breaking through the current levels," said one trader.
